end.summary:
Food miles lesson covered local versus distant food sources.
Rohan linked greater distance with greater fuel use and pollution.
They practised comparing nearby spinach with Shimla apples.
Rohan gave a mostly accurate definition of food miles after prompts.
Teach-back was not passed; effects on freshness and transport needed more explanation.
end.parentNote: Asha practised defining food miles and comparing foods by travel distance, fuel, pollution, cost, and freshness. Rohan used the idea that nearby food travels less distance and needs less fuel, and later explained that distant food may need ice to stay fresh. They mixed up or repeated parts of the explanation, but gave a clearer definition later in the lesson. At home, ask them to compare two foods and name which travelled farther, then give one effect of that distance.
